• Makes regular visits to company worksites (usually weekly) to interact with employees and build relationships of trust and friendship motivated by Christian faith.

• Visits employees or immediate family members wherever care can be expressed and help given: hospitals, nursing homes, funeral homes, family residences, or other sites.

• May provide confidential pastoral discussions for problem issues of employees and their immediate family members including, but not limited to family matters, divorce, serious illness, care of aging parents, death and grief recovery, parenting, financial situations that may include debt discussions, budgeting, and other life issues related to financial stress, as well as any other personal issues. Provides referral service and acts as coordinator for specialized assistance to employees and/or immediate family members with specific needs.

• May assist in the planning, conduct or attend funerals for employees or immediate family members, including follow-up support and encouragement to immediate family members during the grief period.

• May make jail visits to employees and immediate family members.

• Works with companies to serve notifications of death and serious injuries to families and other employees, encouraging those impacted by various tragedies.

• May provide post-termination care for laid-off or terminated employees in order to foster a smooth transition to another work environment.

• May facilitate, but not lead, spiritual enrichment activities, as an employee-sponsored and led activity will usually be more fruitful than a chaplain led event.

• Provides, as appropriate/requested, literature and other resources to assist company employees with life issues.

• Represents companies to clients/customers where it would be appropriate to ministry services involved (i.e., serious illness, accidents, traumatic events, and funerals).

• Participates in new employee orientation to explain the Employee Care Service and the role of the Chaplain Team.

• With Executive Director of Operations (EDO) permission, responds positively and assertively to other duties and services requested by executive leadership of companies, within the scope of the Letter of Agreement between MCHAP Chaplains and the company.

Requirements
1. Has ability to work as member of interdisciplinary group and in an interfaith setting. Possesses ability to accept different lifestyles, cultures, beliefs, and values.

2. Skills to effectively listen and interact with clients, employees, and their families. Skills to deliver community presentations. Skills to deal effectively with family members and staff under stressful circumstances. High regard for the dignity and worth of clients, employees and their families. Skills to cope with stressful situations and able to document accurately according to standards.

3. Spiritual maturity and commitment to a Christian lifestyle and to MCHAPs Ministry values. Incorporates Christian values and beliefs in day-to-day activities and in the performance of job duties. Has a fundamental understanding of the Holy Bible and its proper application. Attests to a saving faith in Jesus Christ and actively participates in a biblically based church.

4. Demonstrated ability to interact professionally with diplomacy, patience, and courtesy with diverse groups; ability to establish and maintain effective and cooperative working relationships while providing exceptional customer service. Ability to make administrative and procedural decisions and judgments on sensitive, confidential issues.

5. Demonstrated excellent oral and written communication skills to communicate and interact effectively with leadership, colleagues, employees, and families. Ability to maintain emotional stability to cope with human suffering, emergencies, and other stresses.

6. Demonstrated skill in analyzing information to define and follow up on problems or objectives. Ability to identify solutions and solve problems. Demonstrated skill in interpreting policy and procedures related to the position and keeping others informed.

7. Demonstrated computer proficiency using Google Suites, Microsoft Office, or other equivalent software, internet, email messaging, and web-based software applications. Ability to understand and learn new technology programs.

8. Must have active state driver’s license and state minimum auto insurance (state(s) where servicing clients).

Conditions of Employment
Must pass a pre-employment background check.

Work Environment
This is a remote position in the field, and the work environment is dependent upon the clients’ worksite. Work environments can include manufacturing, hospitals, office buildings, and funeral homes with differing levels of temperature, noise, and light exposure.

Job Description

Join the Oklahoma Department of Emergency Management (OEM)

Make a difference every day in Oklahoma’s safety and resilience.

About OEM

The Oklahoma Department of Emergency Management (OEM) is a dynamic state agency dedicated to preparing for, responding to, recovering from, and mitigating emergencies and disasters across the State of Oklahoma. OEM plays a key role in statewide public safety by coordinating emergency planning, community preparedness, response operations, disaster recovery, and long-term hazard mitigation with local, tribal, state, and federal partners. The agency also maintains the State Emergency Operations Center (SEOC), providing centralized coordination during critical events and serving more than 300 local emergency managers across the state.

Why Work at OEM?

At OEM, you’ll be part of a mission-driven team that strengthens communities before, during, and after disasters. Whether it’s coordinating response efforts during severe weather, assisting communities with hazard mitigation planning, or providing critical support during emergencies, OEM employees serve with purpose and impact.

Benefits & Perks

As a full-time state employee with OEM, you receive:

  • Competitive state retirement benefits with employer matching
  • 11 paid holidays each year
  • A generous benefit allowance to offset the cost of health, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance premiums for employees and their eligible dependents
  • Opportunities for professional growth and cross-agency collaboration
  • Priority interview consideration for U.S. veterans with appropriate certification
    • Veterans with certification letters from the Office of Management and Enterprise Services’ Office of Veteran Placement are entitled to an interview for any position for which they meet minimum qualifications.

Who We’re Looking For

We seek motivated, adaptable professionals who:

  • Are committed to public service and community preparedness
  • Can work effectively in team environments and high-pressure situations
  • Are resourceful in problem-solving and coordinating across diverse partners

About the Position

We are seeking a Resilience Program Specialist providing support to our Resilience Division area. This position is located in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma.

This position is a regular, full-time position governed by the Oklahoma Civil Service system and subject to the Civil Service and Human Capital Modernization Act. Employment in this role is covered by applicable Civil Service Rules, policies, and procedures.

This position is subject to a required 12-month trial period, during which performance, conduct, and overall suitability for continued employment will be evaluated in accordance with Civil Service Rules.

Position Summary

Under the direction of the State Hazard Mitigation Officer, this position performs professional-level emergency management and resilience program work supporting the administration of Federal Emergency Management Agency Hazard Mitigation Assistance and related resilience initiatives. The Resilience Program Specialist provides technical assistance, grant coordination, project review, financial monitoring, and programmatic support to state, local, and tribal jurisdictions in furtherance of hazard mitigation and disaster resilience objectives.

This position assists with mitigation project development, grant administration, mitigation planning, compliance monitoring, applicant coordination, and disaster recovery support activities in accordance with state and federal regulations and FEMA guidance. Responsibilities include supporting hazard mitigation planning activities led by the agency’s Emergency Management Planner, reviewing project applications, coordinating reimbursements, preparing program reports, and facilitating operational coordination with local jurisdictions, FEMA personnel, and internal agency divisions.

Core Work Responsibilities

Hazard Mitigation Grant Administration

Support administration of Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA) and resilience-related grant programs in accordance with state and federal requirements.

  • Assist in administration of FEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance programs, including Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP), Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC), Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA), and related resilience initiatives
  • Review and support preparation of project applications and associated documentation for submission within established deadlines
  • Coordinate with FEMA personnel, applicants, contractors, and partner agencies regarding mitigation program requirements and project administration activities
  • Provide technical assistance regarding grant requirements, eligibility, application development, reimbursement procedures, and compliance expectations
  • Advise sub-applicants on integrating FEMA Community Lifelines (specifically Energy, Water Systems, and Safety and Security) and future-conditions climate/weather modeling into project narratives to maximize competitiveness in federal review panels
  • Maintain grant and project information required to support program administration, reporting, mitigation planning, and agency decision-making
  • Identify application, eligibility, documentation, or compliance concerns and elevate issues requiring policy interpretation or management determination to the State Hazard Mitigation Officer

Project Review, Financial Coordination & Compliance Monitoring

Support financial management, compliance review, and project monitoring activities associated with mitigation grant programs.

  • Review reimbursement requests, supporting documentation, invoices, procurement records, and financial information for compliance with state and federal requirements
  • Assist with reconciliation of project expenditures, payments, and grant funding activities
  • Monitor project schedules, periods of performance, reporting deadlines, and project completion requirements
  • Support quarterly reporting, budget tracking, amendment coordination, and closeout activities for mitigation grant programs
  • Monitor compliance with federal grant requirements, including procurement standards, documentation requirements, environmental and historic preservation considerations, and applicable FEMA guidance
  • Document deficiencies, unresolved issues, corrective-action requirements, and applicant follow-up activities.
  • Coordinate with Finance, Grants, applicants, contractors, and FEMA personnel to address financial or programmatic documentation concerns.
  • Elevate questioned costs, significant compliance concerns, project delays, or unresolved deficiencies to the State Hazard Mitigation Officer or other appropriate program authority
  • Maintain complete and organized project records supporting reimbursement, monitoring, reporting, audit readiness, and closeout

Applicant Technical Assistance & Project Coordination

Provide technical assistance and coordination support to applicants and stakeholders throughout the mitigation project lifecycle.

  • Assist local, tribal, and state jurisdictions with mitigation project applications, project modifications, requests for information, and grant administration activities
  • Provide guidance regarding FEMA mitigation program requirements, documentation standards, and project implementation expectations
  • Coordinate meetings, workshops, and applicant assistance activities related to mitigation and resilience programs
  • Support communication and coordination between applicants, FEMA personnel, OEM divisions, and partner agencies
  • Provide advanced technical guidance to non-traditional sub-applicants, private non-profits, and infrastructure cooperatives regarding local government sponsorship requirements and eligibility boundaries under HMA guidelines
  • Assist applicants in identifying documentation, technical data, engineering information, environmental review materials, benefit-cost information, and other supporting materials needed for application development or project administration
  • Track applicant requests, outstanding documentation, FEMA requests for information, project modifications, and other required follow-up actions
  • Maintain professional working relationships with local officials, tribal governments, applicants, contractors, and partner agencies
  • Refer questions involving planning ownership, policy determinations, legal interpretation, or final program decisions to the State Hazard Mitigation Officer, Emergency Management Planner, or other designated authority

Hazard Mitigation Planning Support and Resilience Coordination

Provide technical, programmatic, data, and stakeholder support for hazard mitigation planning activities led by the agency’s designated planning authorities.

  • Support the Emergency Management Planner and State Hazard Mitigation Officer in the development, review, update, and implementation of the State Hazard Mitigation Plan and related mitigation planning products.
  • Provide current Hazard Mitigation Assistance program information, project data, grant trends, applicant needs, implementation status, and subject-matter expertise for use in mitigation planning activities.
  • Compile, organize, validate, and provide mitigation project information requested for planning analyses, capability assessments, risk-reduction reporting, plan updates, and implementation monitoring.
  • Assist with stakeholder outreach, meeting coordination, workshop logistics, documentation, and follow-up activities associated with state and local hazard mitigation planning.
  • Participate in planning meetings, workshops, working groups, public-engagement activities, and review sessions as a mitigation grant and project subject-matter resource.
  • Support communication and coordination with state agencies, local jurisdictions, tribal governments, federal partners, and other stakeholders participating in mitigation planning activities.
  • Assist with tracking progress on mitigation actions, grant-supported projects, resilience initiatives, and other implementation activities identified in approved plans.
  • Provide information regarding available mitigation funding, project eligibility, application cycles, grant requirements, and implementation considerations to support planning decisions.
  • Review draft planning materials, when requested, for consistency with current grant requirements, project information, and mitigation program operations.
  • Support local and tribal jurisdictions by connecting mitigation planning priorities with potential funding opportunities and project-development resources.
  • Maintain documentation of assigned planning-support activities and provide required information to the Emergency Management Planner or State Hazard Mitigation Officer.
  • Assist with integration of relevant mitigation project information into preparedness, recovery, resilience, and continuity initiatives.
  • Support, but do not independently direct, approve, maintain, or assume ownership of agency hazard mitigation plans or planning processes.

Disaster Operations and Emergency Response Support

Support emergency management operations and disaster-related activities during emergency events and activations.

  • Support State Emergency Operations Center activities during emergency activations and disaster events as assigned
  • Participate in disaster recovery coordination, field-support assignments, and operational response activities as needed
  • Assist with disaster-related reporting, documentation, operational coordination, and information-management activities
  • Support continuity of mitigation and resilience program operations during disaster events and recovery operations
  • Gather, organize, validate, and communicate information regarding disaster impacts, damaged infrastructure, applicant needs, mitigation opportunities, and project status
  • Coordinate with Operations, Recovery, Individual Assistance, Public Assistance, GIS, Finance, Grants, and other agency functions as assigned
  • Support field assessments, applicant outreach, recovery briefings, and mitigation-related technical assistance following disaster events
  • Maintain accurate and timely records of assigned operational activities, contacts, issues, decisions, and follow-up requirements
  • Operate effectively in high-tempo and rapidly changing operational environments during emergency situations
  • Perform duties within the assigned incident-management structure and comply with established reporting relationships and operational procedures

Program Improvement, Reporting and Organizational Support

Support continuous improvement of mitigation programs, operational workflows, applicant services, and organizational readiness.

  • Assist with development and maintenance of reports, guidance documents, procedures, job aids, templates, and operational materials related to mitigation and resilience programs.
  • Identify opportunities to improve workflows, applicant services, reporting processes, project monitoring, and operational efficiency.
  • Maintain awareness of FEMA policy updates, Hazard Mitigation Assistance guidance changes, regulatory developments, and emerging resilience practices.
  • Evaluate the effect of policy or guidance changes on assigned grant-administration and applicant-support activities.
  • Support training activities and provide programmatic assistance to agency staff, applicants, and stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with internal divisions and external partners to support statewide resilience and mitigation initiatives.
  • Compile program data and prepare routine and special reports regarding applications, awards, expenditures, project status, applicant assistance, compliance issues, and program outcomes.
  • Support implementation of approved corrective actions resulting from audits, monitoring, after-action reviews, program evaluations, or management direction.
  • Maintain and improve tracking tools used to monitor applications, projects, deadlines, expenditures, compliance requirements, and applicant communications.
  • Recommend updates to procedures, templates, guidance, and workflows based on recurring issues, applicant feedback, monitoring results, or federal policy changes.
  • Provide grant and project information requested for agency planning, reporting, legislative inquiries, executive briefings, and performance measurement.
  • Participate in training, exercises, workshops, and professional-development activities that strengthen mitigation and emergency-management capabilities.

Other duties as assigned.

Education and Experience

Education and Experience requirements at this level consist of a bachelor’s degree in business, public administration or urban planning plus one year of qualifying experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience, substituting one year of experience in a technical capacity in emergency preparedness planning or emergency management operations, or in public assistance or disaster recovery operations at the local, state or federal level for each year of the required education plus one additional year of qualifying experience.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Knowledge of:

  • Emergency management, disaster recovery, hazard mitigation, and resilience principles and practices.
  • FEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance programs, grant-administration processes, project lifecycles, and resilience initiatives.
  • State and federal laws, rules, regulations, and guidance related to disaster recovery, mitigation, grants management, and emergency assistance programs.
  • FEMA Benefit-Cost Analysis software and methodologies, including data inputs required for infrastructure and other mitigation projects.
  • Financial management, reimbursement processing, grant monitoring, compliance review, and audit-readiness principles.
  • Project development, project implementation, operational coordination, and public-administration practices.
  • The role of hazard mitigation planning in establishing statewide and local risk-reduction priorities.
  • The distinction between supporting hazard mitigation planning and holding formal responsibility for plan development, maintenance, approval, or compliance.
  • Mitigation planning processes, resilience concepts, preparedness activities, and plan-implementation monitoring.
  • Local, tribal, state, and federal stakeholder roles in mitigation planning and Hazard Mitigation Assistance programs.
  • Environmental and historic preservation requirements applicable to federally funded mitigation projects.
  • Federal procurement, documentation, record-retention, and grant-compliance requirements.
  • Documentation management, operational reporting, data validation, and records-retention practices.
  • Microsoft 365 and standard office productivity applications.

Skills in:

  • Reviewing and organizing financial, operational, technical, planning-support, and grant-related documentation.
  • Coordinating multiple projects, reporting deadlines, applicant needs, and operational priorities simultaneously.
  • Providing applicant technical assistance and mitigation program support.
  • Conducting compliance monitoring, reimbursement review, project tracking, and operational reporting activities.
  • Compiling project, grant, and program data to support hazard mitigation planning and implementation monitoring.
  • Preparing reports, correspondence, guidance materials, technical summaries, and operational documentation.
  • Conducting meetings, workshops, applicant briefings, and stakeholder coordination activities.
  • Identifying and communicating application, project, compliance, documentation, and coordination concerns.
  • Maintaining accurate project records, grant files, tracking systems, and stakeholder communications.
  • Supporting cross-functional planning and recovery activities without assuming authority assigned to designated program owners.

Ability to:

  • Interpret and apply FEMA guidance, regulations, policies, and emergency-management procedures.
  • Analyze grant documentation, reimbursement requests, project information, and supporting records to identify compliance concerns or deficiencies.
  • Review and interpret engineering feasibility studies, watershed-flow simulations, geospatial risk data, and other technical information to assess consistency with federal eligibility standards.
  • Compile and present grant, project, implementation, and stakeholder information in support of hazard mitigation planning activities.
  • Communicate effectively with applicants, public officials, tribal governments, stakeholders, contractors, and partner agencies in written and verbal formats.
  • Establish and maintain effective working relationships with applicants, FEMA personnel, agency staff, and partner organizations.
  • Coordinate and support mitigation, preparedness, recovery, resilience, and planning-related activities within assigned authority.
  • Work collaboratively with the Emergency Management Planner and State Hazard Mitigation Officer while respecting established program ownership and decision-making responsibilities.
  • Anticipate, identify, and address operational, compliance, documentation, and coordination issues.
  • Prepare and review complex reports, grant documentation, project records, and operational materials.
  • Prioritize assignments and maintain accurate work while managing multiple concurrent projects and deadlines.
  • Recognize matters requiring policy interpretation, planning authority, management direction, or formal approval and elevate them appropriately.
  • Operate effectively under pressure and adapt to rapidly changing priorities and operational conditions during disaster events.

Emergency Response Role

Provide operational support during emergency management activations, disaster recovery activities, and resilience coordination efforts.

  • Support State Emergency Operations Center operations and disaster-related coordination during emergency activations and disaster events
  • Participate in field deployments, operational coordination assignments, mitigation-support activities, and disaster recovery operations as assigned
  • Assist with disaster-related reporting, documentation, field information, and operational information-management activities
  • Support continuity of mitigation and resilience program operations during high-tempo disaster events
  • Provide grant, project, applicant, and mitigation information needed to support operational and recovery decision-making
  • Assist with identification and documentation of potential hazard mitigation opportunities following disaster events
  • Coordinate assigned activities with the established incident-management structure and appropriate program owners
  • Operate effectively in rapidly changing operational environments involving extended hours and emergency-response conditions

Systems and Tools

Mitigation & Grant Management Systems

  • FEMA GO
  • FEMA Grants Portal
  • Hazard mitigation grant tracking systems
  • Grant reimbursement and reporting systems
  • Benefit-Cost Analysis tools and supporting technical resources

Documentation & Reporting Tools

  • Microsoft Excel
  • Microsoft Outlook
  • Microsoft Teams
  • SharePoint
  • ArcGIS Pro / GIS Mapping Software
  • Document management and operational reporting systems
  • Project, action, milestone, and planning-support tracking tools

Operational Coordination Tools

  • WebEOC or comparable situational awareness and emergency management coordination systems
  • Virtual meeting and stakeholder coordination platforms
  • Field data-collection and operational communication tools

Requirements and Work Conditions

Travel: Frequent in-state travel and occasional out-of-state travel may be required in support of mitigation coordination activities, applicant meetings, trainings, disaster operations, field assignments, or emergency deployments. Travel may approach 50% during disaster operations or high-volume grant cycles.

Working Conditions:

  • Standard office environment during normal operations
  • Frequent computer-based work involving grant review, reporting, documentation management, and operational coordination activities
  • Frequent interaction with applicants, local officials, tribal governments, FEMA personnel, contractors, and partner agencies
  • May require participation in SEOC operations, field assignments, meetings, workshops, or disaster-related deployments
  • Work may involve extended hours, rapidly changing priorities, and high-volume workloads during grant cycles or disaster operations
  • Duties may require balancing applicant-service needs, federal deadlines, project requirements, and emergency assignments
  • Work is performed within established program authorities, policies, planning responsibilities, and supervisory direction

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to travel to meetings, field locations, applicant sites, and disaster-affected areas as needed
  • Ability to conduct field coordination activities in varying environmental conditions
  • Prolonged periods of sitting and computer-based work
  • Ability to inspect or observe project locations and damaged areas when assigned
  • Ability to carry routine field materials, records, and equipment consistent with assigned duties

Special Requirements:

  • Must possess a valid Oklahoma driver license at the time of appointment and be willing and able to perform all job-related travel associated with the position.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain required FEMA Independent Study and NIMS/ICS training.
  • Must maintain confidentiality of sensitive grant, applicant, planning, financial, and operational information.
  • Must be able to work effectively under pressure and manage multiple concurrent projects, deadlines, and operational priorities.
  • Must be willing and able to work extended or irregular hours during emergency activations and disaster operations.

Preferences

Preference may be given to candidates who possess:

  • Experience supporting FEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance (HMA), disaster recovery, resilience, or grants management programs
  • Experience working within emergency management, public safety, government, environmental planning, or disaster recovery environments
  • Experience reviewing reimbursement requests, procurement documentation, grant applications, or compliance documentation
  • Experience supporting mitigation planning, resilience initiatives, or hazard reduction programs
  • Experience conducting stakeholder coordination, workshops, trainings, or applicant assistance activities
  • FEMA Professional Development Series (PDS) completion or related FEMA mitigation and emergency management training
  • Active pursuit or possession of Associate Emergency Manager (AEM), Certified Emergency Manager (CEM), or Certified Floodplain Manager (CFM) designation, or documented completion of FEMA Advanced Benefit-Cost Analysis or HMA Progress Report training courses

Other Relevant Information

title: MEP Director
description:
Celebrated as one of Minnesota’s Top Workplaces! Knutson Construction is accepting applications for a MEP Director to join our team in Minneapolis, MN.

“Together We Make Dreams Real” – that is our purpose as a company and we exist to work in concert with each other, owners, design professionals and trade partners to make the journey as stress-free as possible. Together, we’ve created a dynamic, fun, inspiring environment where we can be ourselves and grow each day. Knutson is deeply committed to cultivating and upholding diversity throughout our workforce, relationships, and communities. We recognize the utmost importance of continually advancing our comprehension of diversity, equity, and inclusion as transformative forces within our work, industry, and company values.

At Knutson, opportunities to shine happen daily. We value what makes you different and empower you to act on your ideas.

As the Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) Director, you will develop MEP strategies and plans in alignment with company objectives, while actively embracing Knutson’s Zero Incident Safety Culture. This role is responsible for overseeing and directing all mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) aspects of construction projects, while ensuring all MEP systems are designed, installed, and commissioned according to contractual specifications, budgets, schedules and required regulations.

In this key leadership role, you will deliver high-quality outcomes by applying your technical expertise collaboratively with project team members, while effectively communicating and acting as a liaison for trade partners, project teams, and clients.

This leader will deliver The Knutson Experience (TKE), ensuring our owners, design partners, subcontractors, and employees feel Assured, Inspired, and Appreciated.

THE KEY JOB RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO:
Safety Management:

• Champion Knutson’s Zero Incident Safety Culture through pre-planning and proactive measures.
• Oversee and help enforce safety standards on MEP construction activities through audits, training and site visits, ensuring a safe working environment for all personnel.
• Ensure all MEP systems adhere to local, state, and national safety codes and standards, such as those set by the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA), Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), and American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE).
• Participation and completion in scheduled and applicable safety training, as determined by the company.

      Design and Planning:

      • Collaborate with the design team to ensure MEP systems are integrated effectively with the architectural and structural elements.
      • Review and offer guidance on MEP designs and plans.
      • Ensure the MEP design team provides accurate specifications and drawings.
      • Provide MEP expertise while participating in project pursuits and client interviews.
      • Collaborate with the preconstruction team to ensure thorough cost analysis and estimate coordination.
      • Utilize technical knowledge to provide creative alternative solutions to design and budget challenges.
      • Serve as the subject matter expert to estimating and project management teams on all MEP topics, issues and best practices.
      • Oversee the creation of scopes of work for all MEP bid packages and equipment.

      Project Leadership and Oversight:
      • Lead and provide MEP expertise on construction projects, from design through completion.
      • Ensure MEP systems are planned, designed, and executed in compliance with project contracts, local, state, and national building codes, regulations and environmental standards.
      • Provide leadership and direction to MEP professionals, designers, contractors, and subcontractors.
      • Supervise the construction of all MEP scopes of work, ensuring work is performed in accordance with project schedules and budgets.
      • Monitor the progress of MEP work and address any issues related to delays, quality, and compliance.
      • Facilitate resolutions on any MEP issues affecting the project.
      • Stay updated with current MEP construction practices, industry trends, and regulations to ensure ongoing compliance.
      • Effectively plan for and manage risk mitigation through the project life cycle
      • Lead negotiations on MEP-related pricing and change orders with contractors and equipment manufacturers.

      Budget and Cost Management:
      • Prepare and manage MEP project budgets, ensuring costs are controlled (including estimating costs for materials, labor, and MEP equipment) and projects are completed within financial plans.
      • Oversee procurement of materials and MEP subcontractors.
      • Monitor material deliveries and ensure equipment meets quality standards and specifications.
      • Regularly track and update pricing data base for key market sectors.
      • Proactively determine new methods of construction that provides added value at a reduced cost.

      Coordination and Communication:
      • Coordinate with other project departments to ensure integration of MEP systems with other aspects of construction.
      • Serve as the point of contact for all MEP-related issues on the project.
      • Maintain regular communication with clients, consultants, subcontractors, and vendors to ensure expectations are met.
      • Advise on MEP-related logistics, planning, and procurement of materials and equipment.
      • Effectively communicate and partner with various departments to deliver and enhance MEP capabilities across the company, including VDC, self-perform, and the equipment yard.
      • Effectively inform leadership and project teams on MEP-related project updates and trends.

      Quality Control:
      • Ensure that MEP systems meet the highest standards of quality and meet all industry and regulatory compliance standards.
      • Participate with project team for critical pre-work meetings and first work inspections.
      • Conduct site inspections to ensure work is completed according to design and quality specifications.
      • Address any deficiencies or issues promptly to maintain quality standards.

      Team Leadership:
      • Build and grow organizational MEP capabilities and a collaborative, high-performing team to support MEP services.
      • Hire, train, and develop employees to enhance Knutson’s MEP capabilities.
      • Manage performance and provide coaching to improve team skills and impact.
      • Lead and mentor staff supporting MEP deliverables, ensuring effective communication and collaboration among team members.
      • Provide strong communication of MEP project requirements, schedules and expectations.
      • Investigate and implement innovative MEP technologies and sustainable practices to improve project efficiency and reduce environmental impact.
      • Educate and inform other departments (VDC, business development, preconstruction, equipment yard, self-perform) of current and emerging MEP capabilities, innovations and services.
      • Establish and grow relationships with capable MEP subcontractors and designers positioning Knutson to deliver on a variety of projects.
      • Establish and grow relationships in the AEC industry, representing and positioning Knutson for future work opportunities.

      REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
      • Possess robust knowledge of mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems and related regulations and codes.
      • Proven track record of leading MEP initiatives on large, complex projects.
      • Demonstrate strong risk management and risk mitigation skills.
      • Experience in the planning and construction of commercial construction.
      • Thorough knowledge of all aspects of construction (technology, equipment, methods), schedule, cost, safety, and quality.
      • Experience in effectively leading or organization teams to achieve outcomes.
      • Effective communication and interpersonal skills with excellent organizational and planning skills.
      • Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to work in a collaborative team environment.
      • Strong problem-solving abilities and attention to detail.
      • Excellent communication and negotiation skills.
      • Able to attend conferences and seminars to maintain licensure for MEP continuing education.
      • Ability to travel and visit job sites on a regular basis to effectively oversee MEP-related deliverables.
      • The following Professional Certifications/Licenses are recognized as beneficial for this role: LEED, PE License, CEM, PMP, BSI, BICSI, OSHA-30.
      • Experience in Knutson’s major market sectors of healthcare, education, and science & technology is preferred.

      Minimum Education and/or Experience Requirements:
      • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, or Civil Engineering; Construction Management or related field.
      • Minimum of 10 years of commercial mechanical / electrical construction, design experience, or project management experience with an MEP focus.

      Additional Benefits & Perks

      • Competitive Pay
      • Performance Based Career Advancement
      • Medical, Dental and Vision
      • Health Savings Account with employer contribution
      • Flexible Spending Account
      • Paid Time Off
      • Life and Long-Term Disability Benefit with no premium cost to employee
      • Mentorship Program
      • Tuition Reimbursement
      • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
      • Employee Referral Bonus Program
      • Flex Fridays
      • 401k w/Company Match
      • Annual Discretionary Bonus Program
      • Successful Annual Discretionary Profit-Sharing Program
      • Paid Parental Leave

      Projected Minimum Base Salary per year $150,000

      Projected Maximum Base Salary per year $200,000

title: Købsbehandler
description:
Leder du efter et spændende job, hvor dine evner inden for købsmatch og fakturahåndtering kan udfolde sig? Kan du sikre korrekt behandling af leverandørfakturaer og håndtering af pris- og mængdeafvigelser? Og er du klar til at tage ansvar for opfølgning og afslutning af sager? I STARK Huset søger vi lige nu en engageret købsmatch medarbejder, der ønsker at bidrage til stabile købsprocesser og høj datakvalitet i STARK.

Din rolle som købsbehandler i STARK
Du bliver en del af købsmatch-funktionen på Hovedkontoret i Viby J, Aarhus, hvor vi arbejder målrettet med korrekt behandling af leverandørfakturaer og afvigelser i tæt samarbejde med resten af organisationen. Som STARKs nye købsmatch medarbejder får du en vigtig rolle i at sikre kvalitet, overholdelse af interne kontroller og en professionel dialog på tværs af forretningen. Det betyder, at du:

  • Arbejder med korrekt behandling af leverandørfakturaer og har forståelse for 3-vejs match, GR/IR og afvigelser
  • Afklarer og regulerer varemodtagelsesfejl
  • Håndterer pris- og mængdeafvigelser
  • Varetager varemodtagelse af direkte leverancer
  • Kontrollerer bilag, hvor fakturering mangler eller er fejlagtig
  • Følger op på relevante rapporter
  • Indgår i professionel og løsningsorienteret dialog med kollegaer og leverandører omkring korrektioner og afklaringer
  • Samarbejder tæt med salg, logistik og indkøb
  • Bidrager til procesforbedringer, høj datakvalitet og stabile købsprocesser
  • Arbejder struktureret med høj kvalitet og følger sager til afslutning
  • Anvender systemer som Apekt4 i det daglige arbejde og snart også SAP

Vores nye Købsbehandler

Du vil blive en del af at sikre, at vi efterlever vores værdier. Det betyder, at vi udviser ordentlighed, passion og stolthed overfor vores kunder, samarbejdspartnere, leverandører og kollegaer i det daglige arbejde.
For at trives i rollen er det vigtigt, at du tager ejerskab over dine opgaver og har fokus på det gode samarbejde. Du arbejder struktureret, har forretningsforståelse og evner at føre en professionel og løsningsorienteret dialog.
Den rette kandidat for os kan have relevant erfaring med købsmatch, fakturahåndtering eller lignende opgaver.

Det er vigtigt, at vi er tæt på vores kollegaer i STARK forretningerne for at forstå deres behov og muligheder. Kendskab til arbejdsområdet kan derfor være en fordel, men alternativt er interessen og nysgerrigheden for at lære vores forretning afgørende.

Hvis du kan genkende dig selv i ovenstående, vil vi sørge for en grundig oplæring, så du bliver klædt på med den nødvendige viden, kompetencer og kendskab til arbejdsområdet, der skal til for, at du kan yde dit bedste og opnå gode resultater i rollen.

En del af STARK holdet
Hos STARK mener vi, at forskellighed er værdifuldt og er af den overbevisning, at hvert enkelt medarbejders bidrag er essentielt for virksomhedens fortsatte udvikling. Derfor er vi også stolte af, at vi kan måle stor arbejdsglæde og loyalitet blandt vores medarbejdere, hvilket vi også håber, at du vil opleve som vores nye købsmatch medarbejder. Udover gode arbejdsforhold tilbyder vi personalepolitikker og vilkår, der tilgodeser dig som medarbejder i tråd med STARKs værdi om ordentlighed.

Skal du med på STARK holdet?
Så send os en kort beskrivelse af hvorfor du skal være en del af holdet, som købsbehandler i STARK-Huset, samt dit CV via linket senest den 14. august 2026. Vi inviterer til samtaler løbende og afslutter processen, når vi har fundet den rette kandidat.

Stillingen er en fuldtidsstilling på 37 timer og vi håber, at du kan starte snarest.

Har du spørgsmål til jobbet, eller er du nysgerrig på at vide mere om STARK Huset som din kommende arbejdsplads, er du velkommen til at kontakte Purchase Processing Manager Tinna Seliger på telefon +45 27 28 85 67

Vi ser frem til at modtage din ansøgning.

___________________________________________________

Om STARK

STARK er Danmarks største forhandler og distributør af byggematerialer med flere end 80 forretninger i Danmark og Grønland. STARK tilbyder også faglig rådgivning og en lang række services til både entreprenører og professionelle håndværkere. Virksomheden beskæftiger over 2.400 medarbejdere og er en del af STARK Group, der med flere end 18.500 medarbejdere og 1.050 forretninger og distributionscentre i Norden, Storbritannien, Tyskland og Østrig, er en førende leverandør af byggematerialer i Europa.

STARK Group har SBTi-godkendte net zero klimamål for 2050. Koncernen har underskrevet FN’s Global Compact principper og er anerkendt af EcoVadis med en Platinum-rating for sin bæredygtighedsindsats.

Vi bygger fremtiden ved at hjælpe andre med at bygge deres.

title: Tree Trimmer
description:
Job Title: Tree Trimmer

Pay Rate Type: Non-Exempt

Creation Date/Revision Date: 04/24/2026

Job Summary:

The Tree Trimmer role is a qualified Line Clearance Tree Trimmer responsible for pruning and removing trees, limbs and shrubs away from power lines to reduce vegetation interference. This role utilizes various types of equipment, tools, and techniques to perform basic tree maintenance while addressing growth patterns and ensuring tree health, and appearance.

Essential Job Duties:

  • Loads vehicles and equipment with manageable size limbs and logs not suited for wood chipping.

  • Trims, removes and/or fells trees using climbing equipment, such as a powered trimmer lift truck, safety belt, climbing line, and ladder. Also works on the ground using hand saws, ground saws, pruners or other applicable tools.

  • Works aloft to cut branches or trunk sections and drop or lower them to the ground with rigging lines.

  • Uses appropriate tools on the ground to fell trees or spars and split them into manageable pieces.

  • Works around hazardous equipment and may work in close proximity to energized power lines while under the direct supervision of a qualified line clearance tree trimmer. Once the prerequisites for qualification have been met, may provide direct supervision of the activities of non-qualified employees working in close proximity to energized conductors.

  • Applies herbicide and growth regulators to brush and stumps. Maintains appropriate application records.

  • Adheres to and helps educate less experienced employees on company policies, procedures, on-the-job safety practices, approved work methods and OSHA regulations.

  • Repairs minor damage to property that occurs on the job site. Escalates situations to General Foreperson’s when necessary and in a timely manner.

  • Feeds brush and debris into woodchipper.

  • Sets up warning signs, barriers, flags, relays hand-signals, directs traffic and other applicable traffic control devices to protect employees and members of the public from hazards in and around the work area. Cooperates with property owner, customer, and emergency personnel when blocking streets or driveways.

  • Conducts vehicle and equipment inspections to ensure proper working conditions. Conducts routine maintenance on company vehicles, equipment and tools. Reports specialized vehicle maintenance or equipment needs to General Foreperson.

  • During emergencies or natural disasters may be required to be on duty and travel outside of regular work location for the duration of the disaster.

  • Support, actively participate, and act in accordance with Wright’s culture of safety and employee ownership.

  • Comply with applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations; maintain knowledge of and follow all company policies and procedures.

  • Maintain regular and punctual attendance at work and meetings.

Other Duties:

  • Drives and operates vehicles and equipment as assigned.

Supervisory Duties:

Knowledge, Skills & Ability Requirements:

  • Must have basic knowledge of trees, including identification, growth habits and arboricultural techniques specific to trimming, pruning, repairing, maintaining and removing, in close proximity to energized conductors.

  • Knowledge and understanding of the American National Standards for Tree Care Operations (ANSI Z133.1-current version) and American National Standards for Proper Pruning (ANSI A300).

  • Ability to adhere and coach employees on company and industry safety requirements.

  • Knowledge of electrical circuits and skilled in reading and understanding of circuit maps.

  • Knowledge of OSHA electric power generation, transmission, and distribution standards, including 29 CFR 1910.269. Ability to determine nominal voltage, proper use of insulated tools near energized parts and distinguish exposed live parts from other parts of electric equipment.

  • Ability to learn quickly and to follow instructions accurately.

  • Must be able to communicate with others and represent Wright Tree Service in a professional manner.

  • Must be able to comprehend and/or read and write both written and verbal job instructions and safety information.

  • Ability to recognize poisonous plants and take proper safeguard against them.

  • Must be able to wear necessary personal protective equipment (PPE) as required.

  • Ability to work long hours and overtime during emergencies (including holidays, weekends, storm work) and will be subject to call-out work.

  • Demonstrate knowledge and trained to perform tree and bucket rescue.

Cargo: Tree Trimmer

Tipo de salario: No exento

Fecha de creación/Fecha de revisión: 04/24/2026

Resumen del puesto:

El Tree Trimmer es un Qualified Line Clearance Tree Trimmer (podador calificado para el despeje de líneas) responsable de podar y retirar árboles, ramas y arbustos cerca de las líneas eléctricas para reducir la interferencia de la vegetación. La persona en esta función utiliza diversos equipos, herramientas y técnicas para realizar mantenimiento básico de los árboles, teniendo en cuenta los patrones de crecimiento y la salud y apariencia de los árboles.

Funciones esenciales del puesto:

  • Carga vehículos y equipos con ramas y troncos de tamaño manejable que no pueden ser triturados.

  • Poda, retira o tala árboles usando equipos de escalada, como camión con elevador de poda, cinturón de seguridad, cuerda de escalada y escalera. También trabaja en el suelo utilizando sierras manuales, sierras de uso en el suelo, podadoras u otras herramientas aplicables.

  • Trabaja en altura para cortar ramas o secciones de tronco y bajarlas al suelo con cuerdas de izado.

  • Utiliza herramientas apropiadas en el suelo para talar árboles o troncos y dividirlos en piezas fáciles de manipular.

  • Trabaja cerca de equipos peligrosos y puede desempeñarse en proximidad a líneas energizadas bajo la supervisión directa de un Qualified Line Clearance Tree Trimmer (podador calificado para el despeje de líneas). Una vez cumplidos los requisitos para la calificación, puede supervisar directamente las actividades de empleados no calificados que trabajan cerca de conductores energizados.

  • Aplica herbicidas y reguladores de crecimiento a la maleza (brush) y los troncos. Mantiene los registros de aplicación correspondientes.

  • Cumple y ayuda a capacitar a empleados con menos experiencia sobre las políticas de la empresa, los procedimientos, las prácticas de seguridad en el trabajo, los métodos de trabajo aprobados y las normativas de la Administración de Salud Ocupacional (OSHA).

  • Repara daños menores a la propiedad que ocurran en el lugar de trabajo. Informa al General Foreperson de las situaciones que requieran atención, de forma oportuna.

  • Alimenta la trituradora de madera con maleza y residuos.

  • Coloca señales de advertencia, barreras, banderas, transmite señales manuales, dirige el tráfico y utiliza otros dispositivos de control de tráfico según corresponda, para proteger a los empleados y al público de los peligros en y alrededor del área de trabajo. Coopera con los propietarios, clientes y personal de emergencia cuando sea necesario bloquear calles o entradas.

  • Realiza inspecciones de vehículos y equipos para garantizar su correcto funcionamiento. Efectúa el mantenimiento rutinario de los vehículos, equipos y herramientas de la empresa. Informa al General Foreperson. sobre las necesidades de mantenimiento especializado de los vehículos o equipos.

  • Durante emergencias o desastres naturales, puede ser necesario permanecer de servicio y desplazarse fuera del lugar habitual de trabajo durante la duración del evento.

  • Apoya, participa activamente y actúa de acuerdo con la cultura de seguridad y sentido de pertenencia de Wright.

  • Cumple con las leyes, normas y reglamentos federales, estatales y locales aplicables; mantiene el conocimiento y cumplimiento de todas las políticas y procedimientos de la empresa.

  • Mantiene una asistencia regular y puntual al trabajo y a las reuniones.

Otras funciones:

  • Conduce y opera los vehículos y equipos asignados.

Funciones de supervisión:

Conocimientos, habilidades y aptitudes requeridas:

  • Debe tener conocimientos básicos sobre los árboles, incluyendo su identificación, hábitos de crecimiento y técnicas de arboricultura específicas para la poda, el mantenimiento, la reparación y la eliminación de árboles en proximidad a conductores energizados.

  • Conocimiento y comprensión de las normas nacionales estadounidenses para operaciones de cuidado de árboles (ANSI Z133.1 – versión vigente) y de las Normas Nacionales Estadounidenses para la poda adecuada (ANSI A300).

  • Capacidad para cumplir y capacitar a los empleados sobre los requisitos de seguridad de la empresa y del sector.

  • Conocimientos sobre circuitos eléctricos y habilidad para leer e interpretar planos de circuitos.

  • Conocimiento de las normas de generación, transmisión y distribución de energía eléctrica de la OSHA, incluido el artículo 1910.269 del Título 29 del Código de Reglamentaciones Federales (CFR). Capacidad para determinar el voltaje nominal, usar correctamente herramientas aisladas cerca de partes energizadas y distinguir las partes vivas expuestas de otras partes del equipo eléctrico.

  • Capacidad para aprender rápidamente y seguir instrucciones con precisión.

  • Capacidad para comunicarse con otras personas y representar a Wright Tree Service de manera profesional.

  • Capacidad para comprender o leer y escribir tanto las instrucciones laborales como la información de seguridad, en forma escrita y verbal.

  • Capacidad para reconocer plantas venenosas y adoptar las medidas preventivas adecuadas.

  • Debe ser capaz de llevar el equipo de protección personal (PPE) requerido.

  • Capacidad para trabajar jornadas prolongadas y realizar horas extras durante emergencias (incluidos feriados, fines de semana y trabajos por tormentas), estando sujeto a llamadas de emergencia.

  • Conocimiento y formación en rescate en árboles y con elevador aéreo (canasta).

  • Capacidad para operar y mantener todas las herramientas y equipos requeridos.

  • Capacidad para trabajar tanto de forma independiente como en equipo.

Requisitos de formación, certificación y experiencia:

  • Contar con un mínimo de 3 meses de experiencia trabajando en cuadrillas de poda o despeje de árboles, o haber completado con éxito las evaluaciones de habilidades correspondientes.

  • Se prefiere título de educación secundaria o equivalente, aunque no es obligatorio.

  • Debe contar con credenciales vigentes de resucitación cardiopulmonar (CPR), o poder obtenerlas en un plazo de 90 días tras la contratación.

Otros requisitos preferidos:

  • Capacidad para obtener y mantener una licencia de conducir válida o una licencia comercial (según la división y los requisitos del cliente o contrato) y una tarjeta médica emitida por el Departamento de Transporte (Department of Transportation, DOT) conforme a las regulaciones de la FMCSA.

  • Conducir un vehículo con una astilladora u otra unidad remolcada acoplada hacia, desde o dentro del área de trabajo.

  • Mantener la certificación o equivalente en aplicación de herbicidas según lo requieran Wright Tree Service y las leyes locales, estatales y federales.

Este puesto puede requerir las siguientes exigencias y actividades físicas:

  • Flexionarse, estirarse, permanecer de pie, caminar, trepar, levantar, cargar, sujetar, hablar, oír y realizar movimientos repetitivos de manera efectiva. Ocasionalmente alcanzar hacia arriba o hacia abajo.

title: Developer Relations Manager, CAE
description:
We're hiring a Developer Relations Manager to lead strategic engagement across developer ecosystems in rapidly evolving technology domains. In this role, you’ll help develop how NVIDIA partners with software providers, developers, and industry teams to expand the use of our AI and computing platforms. We're looking for someone with strong architectural depth who can guide partner product direction and support developers building on NVIDIA technologies. If you're passionate about influencing the next wave of AI and accelerated computing, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Be Doing:

  • Build and deepen technical expertise in computer-aided engineering (CAE), serving as a technical advocate and trusted resource for developers in industrial engineering, with cross-functional partners to drive adoption of NVIDIA technologies.

  • Demonstrate and integrate NVIDIA’s software stack (tools, SDKs, libraries, NIMs, and blueprints) into real-world partner or developer projects to accelerate adoption.

  • Support developers and partners through onboarding and integration by providing code samples, guides, demo pipelines, and hands-on assistance that enable CAE-specific use cases.

  • Research and monitor developer ecosystem trends to identify opportunities for growth, sharing insights with engineering, product, and marketing teams to improve adoption strategies.

  • Collaborate with partner technical leaders and internal engineering stakeholders to troubleshoot challenges, guide best-practice integrations, and feed technical takeaways back to NVIDIA teams.

What We Need to See:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.

  • 5-8+ years of overall professional experience in software engineering, developer relations, technical partnerships, solutions architect, product management, including hands-on experience crafting and/or deploying software tools for CAE.

  • Experience working with or supporting developer programs, technical ecosystems, or CAE ISVs, or within relevant verticals.

  • Proficiency in developing CAE workflows, software tools for physical simulation,and familiarity with modern software frameworks or SDKs.

  • Comfort collaborating with cross-functional teams to discuss architecture, share feedback, and deliver technical presentations or demos.

  • Ability to manage and implement technical projects, solve integration challenges, and effectively communicate complex ideas to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Strong communication skills and a passion for helping developers innovate with NVIDIA tools and technology.

Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • Experience creating or optimizing vertical-specific technical solutions i.e. simulation tools, virtual twins, and/or solutions for CAE, high-performance computing, applied machine learning, or deep learning.

  • Hands-on familiarity with NVIDIA platforms and frameworks: CUDA-X Libraries, PhysicsNeMo, Omniverse, NeMo, etc.

  • Demonstrated involvement in growing developer communities and supporting technical enablement programs.

  • Skilled in developing systems and tools to measure developer sentiment and track market trends, turning ecosystem insights into practical recommendations that guide product direction and strategic planning.

  • Experience with AI physics models and model architecture including developing, defining, training, and deploying open or proprietary models.

With competitive salaries and a generous benefits package, we are widely considered to be one of the world’s most desirable employers! We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us and, due to outstanding growth, our best-in-class engineering teams are rapidly growing. If you're a creative and autonomous person with a real passion for technology, we want to hear from you.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 152,000 USD - 241,500 USD.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

The Director, Power Market Sector will position Knutson as a general contractor that safely and rapidly delivers complex power generation facilities where safety, schedule, constructability, and owner risk matter most—particularly co-generation and single cycle projects supporting industrial operations and critical infrastructure. This role leads strategic growth, business development, client relationship management, and market expansion for power generation projects, with a primary focus on co-generation, single-cycle, and combined-cycle power facilities, and the continued growth of this sector into larger and more complex generation programs. This role will also pursue utility-support facility and service center project opportunities to provide deep and broad services to match client needs.

The Director is accountable for developing new relationships, driving revenue growth, expanding existing partnerships, developing and owning a business plan and go-to-market strategy, and ensuring the organization captures high‑value work within facilities supporting modern power infrastructure.

The ideal candidate is a strategic leader and market sector expert capable and motivated to deliver The Knutson Experience (TKE) to all clients, employees, and partners, making everyone Knutson works with feel assured, inspired, and appreciated.

Safety

  • Ensure power sector teams and partners understand and uphold safety expectations.

Strategic Leadership

Recommend investments in talent, technology, partnerships, and capabilities to support sustainable expansion.

Business Development and Growth

  • Own the power generation project pipeline and revenue forecasting with explicit focus on co-generation, single-cycle, and combined-cycle projects, while tracking follow-on service center work generated through generation clients and track conversion metrics. Drive pursuit strategy, go/no-go decisions, and development of proposals and presentations.
  • Build, strengthen, and maintain executive-level relationships with utilities, independent power producers (IPPs), EPC firms, OEMs, municipal and cooperative utilities, developers, and other key industry partners and stakeholders.

Leadership and Collaboration

    • Lead with Courage

  • Provide leadership and mentorship to business development, preconstruction, and operations staff engaged in power sector opportunities.
  • Foster collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement across teams.

  • Partner across departments to ensure alignment with sector objectives.

Client & Stakeholder Engagement, Brand Ambassador

  • Serve as the sector’s primary executive point of contact for major clients.
  • Ensure high levels of client satisfaction and promote repeat business.
  • Gather and translate client feedback into actionable improvements and repeatable business.
  • Collaborate and be a leading participant in visibility and brand-building efforts including industry events, speaking engagements, and content creation.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Visionary leadership with strong client-focus.
  • Proven success in Power sector market development and relationship building.
  • Strong understanding of preconstruction, design-build, and construction delivery models.
  • Strong financial acumen and metrics-driven decision-making.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.
  • Knowledge of MEP-intensive systems, commissioning, prefab strategies, and fast-turnover requirements typical of utility-scale clients.
  • Proficiency in CRM and business intelligence tools.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability and willingness to travel to project sites, client offices, conferences, events, and other locations on a regular and reasonable basis to achieve sector business objectives, which may be up to 50% of the role at times, regionally and nationally where opportunities are present.
  • Working knowledge of regulatory and code environments impacting power generation and utility facilities (e.g., OSHA, EPA, NFPA/NEC considerations, and applicable state/local building codes), and ability to integrate code-driven requirements into pursuit and planning.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Architecture, Engineering, or Business; Master’s preferred.

  • Understanding of construction operations, including scheduling, cost drivers, MEP, preconstruction, and risk management.

title: Sr. Business Analyst
description:
About Wealth Enhancement


Wealth Enhancement is an independent wealth management firm with an endless passion for enriching the lives of our clients. Our Practice Management Team has an exciting opportunity available for a Senior Business Analyst. This role will be responsible for supporting the Practice Management Team (PMT) focused on advisor support through team reporting, metrics, business system support (Salesforce Support Org and Actifi), and enablement of scalable workflows through process documentation, data governance, and automation/AI enhanced capabilities. This role provides back-up coverage across core PMT reporting and business systems support and reports to the Director of PMT Operations.

In the spirit of pay transparency, we are excited to share the base salary range for this position is $80,000.00 to $90,000.00, exclusive of bonuses and benefits. We encourage you to apply and provide us with your compensation expectations when you do. We’re big on open conversations, so, let’s have one.

Primary Job Functions

Partner and Support PMT Stakeholders and PMT Initiatives

  • Serve as a business partner to Advisor Services Directors and PMT members to translate requests into clear requirements, prioritization, and deliverables.

  • Own intake for reporting and system requests (triage, scope, success criteria, timelines) and coordinate cross-functional resolution.

  • Prepares standard and consistent reporting for scheduled meetings between Advisor Services Directors, other PMT participants, and Advisor Team Leads.

Reporting & Analytics (monthly, quarterly, ad hoc)

  • Coordinates and prepares monthly Advisor Team reporting, key metrics, and variance analyses.

  • Analyzes and validates results to ensure accuracy, accountability, and data integrity.

  • Perform detailed ad hoc analysis to understand drivers of trends or results.

  • Maintain and enhance repeatable reporting assets and templates; write and maintain procedure documentation and metric definitions.

  • Performs other ad hoc reporting or projects as assigned.

Service Model, Engagement & Performance Reporting

  • Maintain and improve ser model reporting (expected vs. delivered touchpoints by tier, region/department and related roll ups

  • Support engagement scoring processes and reporting outputs used in leadership and operational reviews

  • Partner with stakeholders to identify data gaps, improve classification, and reduce manual effort in recurring reporting

Business Systems Support (ActiFi, Salesforce Support Org)

  • Salesforce Support Org: Support data integrity, user access/permissions questions, and field governance; partner with Helpdesk/Technology for admin changes.

  • Ensure key channels (Salesforce, Support Org, ActiFi, and downstream reporting) are updated with correct and accurate data.

Data Governance, Automation & Enablement

  • Consolidate and maintain PMT data and statistics on an ongoing basis (e.g., NCNM, ECNM, net flows, engagement/activity metrics) across sources.

  • Identify data quality issues and drive resolution with appropriate data owners; implement lightweight controls and reconciliation checks.

  • Support automation/AI initiatives that improve the capture of follow-up items and streamline recurring reporting workflows.

  • Superior verbal and written communication skills; ability to translate analysis into clear recommendations and stakeholder ready materials.

  • Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite – specifically PowerPoint and Excel.

  • Strong knowledge of data platforms and data extraction (Salesforce, Orion preferred).

  • Working knowledge of BI/reporting concepts (Power BI a plus) and comfort with data quality, definitions, and governance

  • Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and provide reliable back-up cover for critical reporting and systems support.

  • FINRA Series 7 & 66 preferred

Comprehensive Benefits Offerings

Our benefits aim to balance four key elements that make life and work meaningful: health and wellness, financial well-being, professional development, and work/life harmony. You may be eligible to participate in the following benefits & development opportunities:

title: Per Diem Virtual Pediatric Speech-Language Pathologist
description:
About Us:

Ladder Health, an innovative virtual care platform built alongside clinicians at Boston Children's Hospital, serves as an end-to-end developmental partner for children (0-6 years old) with developmental delays. Ladder offers an alternative to waitlisted state-based programs or private pay practices, guiding families through our developmental screener, clinical evaluations, and comprehensive virtual care with specialized therapists (PT, OT, SLP). Our platform supports a coordinated care plan with resources, HIPAA-compliant messaging, and integration with pediatric care teams. Ladder partners with pediatricians and community organizations to improve access and quality of care for families.

About You:

  • Self-motivated pediatric Speech-Language Pathologist, ideally with telehealth experience, having worked in Early Intervention, school-based programs, or private practice
  • Experience working with children (0-6) and their caregivers
  • Up-to-date on evidence based practices and enthusiastic about use of technology to facilitate and augment care
  • Passionate about caregiver guided intervention, strengths-based framing and play as therapy, and the impact early intervention support can have on children
  • Flexible schedule to allow for convenient appointment times for busy families (e.g., some availability in early mornings and/or evening, and/or weekends
  • License to practice in Massachusetts required
  • Bilingual professional capabilities is appreciated

Responsibilities:

  • Perform virtual consult/evaluation appointments with children and their families and use clinical decision making to determine need for ongoing support. Thorough review of medical history, developmental concerns, and goals for seeking support.
  • Document clinically sound, personalized care plans and recommend therapy frequency (weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly)
  • Facilitate therapy appointments with child and their caregiver(s). Communicate clearly with caregivers and educate them on activities and exercises so they can work with their child at home.
  • Maintain up-to-date patient records including appointment summaries, progress monitoring, and other documentation
  • Utilize the platform to recommend exercises/activities that caregivers can apply in between appointments to work toward therapy goals
  • Work to improve the platform including review of developmental screener and associated escalation logic, expansion of exercises library, and other enhancements
  • Responsive to the messaging portal to answer questions from users on a predetermined cadence
  • Collaborate with other clinicians to ensure children and their families are receiving holistic care.

Benefits:

  • Chance to work at an innovative, early-stage digital health company, with room for growth and opportunities for advancement
  • Flexible hours with the ability to work part-time
  • Opportunity to mold a new care delivery model and help the access gap for children who need developmental services but are unable to receive them today
  • Hourly salary commensurate with experience

title: General Foreperson - Travel Pod
description:
Salary: $82,160

Division 30

Job Title: General Foreperson

Pay Rate Type: Exempt

Creation Date/Revision Date: 04/24/2026

Job Summary:

The General Foreperson provides support and coaching to the crew to achieve production goals. This role identifies safety hazards and ensures compliance along with task allocation and prioritization of work on the job site as directed by their Project Manager.

Essential Job Duties:

  • Provides direct oversight and supervision of line clearance crew members. Including, but not limited to employee work assignments, interpretation and application of Union Agreements, performance management and coaching in accordance with company policies, procedures, and customer requirements.

  • Adheres to, trains and coaches employees on company policies, procedures, on-the-job safety practices, approved work methods, and OSHA regulations.

  • Conducts necessary safety training, stand downs, and pre-job briefings. Engages Safety Education Training team to coordinate additional training initiatives to address areas of opportunity and concern.

  • Collaborates with Human Resources regarding employment for crew members including, but not limited to, hiring, discipline, separation of employment, leaves of absence – FMLA/ADA, as well as policy overall enforcement. Must understand Form I-9 process and proper interviewing techniques as well as exercise fair and reasonable judgment working through employee relations matters.

  • Obtains and interprets maps from the utility showing work orders to be completed for tree trimming, removals and chemical application. Responsible for understanding drawings and symbols representing types of power lines, voltages, and line equipment per industry standard and assigning daily work orders.

  • Responsible for maintaining records, and reports related to the production of the crew, such as timesheets, work orders, units of work, manhours, distribution of crew assignments and locations.

  • Responsible for controlling costs, including effective use of manpower, work methods, proper amount of trimming, and operation of equipment to meet organizational goals.

  • Works closely with internal departments to support accident investigations, property damage claims, truck breakdowns and workers compensation claims. May be a designated representative to settle minor claims.

  • Conducts vehicle and equipment inspections to ensure proper working conditions. Conducts routine maintenance on company vehicles, equipment and tools and request major repairs and replacements when necessary.

  • Maintains knowledge of new equipment specifications, standard practices and operating procedures.

  • Remains in contact with customers, property owners, general public, other contractors, and utility representatives and governmental agencies 20-30% of the time. Promotes and maintains good customer and public relations through courteous communication on behalf of Wright Tree Service.

  • Works around hazardous equipment and in close proximity to energized power lines.

  • During emergencies or natural disasters may be required to be on duty and travel outside of regular work location for the duration of the disaster. Assists with contacting and coordinating the crew’s response to such work and responsible for determining proper steps necessary to eliminate hazards and trim/remove trees while onsite during emergency response.

  • Support, actively participate, and act in accordance with Wright’s culture of safety and employee ownership.

  • Comply with applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations; maintain knowledge of and follow all company policies and procedures.

  • Maintain regular and punctual attendance at work and meetings.

Other Duties:

  • Drives and operates vehicles and equipment as assigned.

Supervisory Duties:

  • Oversees crew employees.

Knowledge, Skills & Ability Requirements:

  • Possess excellent leadership skills and be able to handle stressful situations along with being able to multi-task.

  • Knowledge of trees, including identification, growth habits and arboricultural techniques specific to trimming, pruning, repairing, maintaining and removing, in close proximity to energized conductors.

  • Excellent customer service and communication skills focused on rapport-building, listening, questioning and patience. Ability to communicate professionally and effectively with the general public, customers and employees at all levels.

  • Knowledge and understanding of the American National Standards for Tree Care Operations (ANSI Z133.1-current version) and American National Standards for Proper Pruning (ANSI A300).

  • Ability to adhere, educate, and enforce company and industry safety requirements.

  • Knowledge of electrical circuits and skilled in reading and understanding of circuit maps.

  • Knowledge of OSHA electric power generation, transmission, and distribution standards, including 29 CFR 1910.269. Ability to determine nominal voltage, proper use of insulated tools near energized parts and distinguish exposed live parts from other parts of electric equipment.

  • Proficient with Microsoft Office products.

  • Must be able to communicate with others and represent Wright Tree Service in a professional manner.

  • Must be able to write, read, and comprehend written and verbal job instructions/information.

  • Ability to recognize poisonous plants and take proper safeguard against them.

  • Must be able to wear necessary personal protective equipment (PPE) as required.

  • Ability to work long hours and overtime during emergencies (including holidays, weekends, storm work) and will be subject to call-out work.

  • Demonstrate knowledge and trained to perform tree and bucket rescue.

  • Ability to operate and service all required tools and equipment.

  • Ability to work both independently and in a group.

Education, Certification & Experience Requirements:

  • Has a minimum of 4-5 years’ experience working on tree trimming or clearing crews or has successfully completed applicable skills assessments.

  • High School diploma or equivalent preferred but not required.

  • Must have valid First-Aid and CPR cards.

  • Ability to obtain and maintain a valid driver’s or commercial driver’s license (dependent upon Division and utility/contract requirements). and DOT medical card in accordance with FMCSA regulations.

Other Preferred Requirements:

  • Drive a vehicle with an attached chipper or other trailing unit to, from or within the work area.

  • Maintain herbicide application certification or equivalent as required by Wright Tree Service and local, state, and federal law.
